name: fix_wrong_http_status_spring
description: Fixes a POST endpoint that wrongly returns 200 instead of 201
prompts: In this Maven Spring Boot project, POST /notes (implemented in src/main/java/com/optarena/notes/NoteController.java) creates a new note and stores it, but it currently returns HTTP 200 OK. Fix it so that a successful creation returns HTTP 201 Created (with the created note as the JSON response body). GET /notes must keep returning HTTP 200 with the list of notes, unchanged. Do not change any other behavior.

test_setup_files.test_notes.py:
import subprocess, sys, time, json, glob, urllib.request, urllib.error

subprocess.run(['mvn', '-o', '-q', 'package', '-DskipTests'], check=True)
jars = [j for j in glob.glob('target/*.jar') if not j.endswith('.original')]
assert jars, 'no runnable jar produced under target/'
srv = subprocess.Popen(['java', '-jar', jars[0]])

def wait_ready():
    for _ in range(40):
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:8080/notes', timeout=1):
                return True
        except (urllib.error.URLError, ConnectionResetError):
            time.sleep(0.5)
    return False

try:
    assert wait_ready(), 'server never became reachable on :8080'

    req = urllib.request.Request(
        'http://127.0.0.1:8080/notes', data=json.dumps({'text': 'hi'}).encode(),
        headers={'Content-Type': 'application/json'}, method='POST')
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=2) as resp:
        assert resp.status == 201, f'expected 201 Created, got {resp.status}'
        created = json.loads(resp.read())
        assert created.get('text') == 'hi', f'unexpected body: {created!r}'

    with urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:8080/notes', timeout=2) as resp:
        assert resp.status == 200, f'expected 200, got {resp.status}'
        body = json.loads(resp.read())
        assert any(n.get('text') == 'hi' for n in body), f'note missing from list: {body!r}'
finally:
    srv.terminate()
    try:
        srv.wait(timeout=10)
    except Exception:
        srv.kill()
print('PASS')
